given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today
given.why: Both loans are lent on 2026-03-02, so they fall due on 03-16, and the job runs on 03-17. Line 29 would fail if they weren't treated as overdue.

The test clock is always set to 10:00Z. A job that worked out 'today' in local time would get the same date in nearly every timezone, so the test would still pass; nothing sets a time near midnight where UTC and local dates differ.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: Only a loan that has never had a reminder is set up. No test has a loan that was reminded on an earlier day, so a job that skipped any loan with a reminder at all, ignoring the date, would pass every test.

then.why: The fake records every accepted reminder, and the test asserts exactly two are there. Skipping the call would leave the list empty.
Each reminder is matched on its memberId, which differs from its loanId, so sending a different member would fail.
The test asserts exactly two rows in the reminders table.
sent_on must be 2026-03-17. That differs from dueOn (03-16), so recording the wrong date would fail.
Nothing in B1 shows the order. The only visible effect is that nothing is recorded after a refusal, which is B3's Then, and B3's test asserts that only the accepted loan was recorded.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on the same day, so loan1 already has today's reminder on the second run.
loan2 is overdue but returned before the job runs.
loan3 is due on 03-17, the day the job runs, which tests the boundary between due and overdue.

then.why: On an array, toMatchObject also checks length, so the fake must hold exactly one reminder, for loan1. A second reminder for loan1, or any reminder for loan2 or loan3, would fail.

given.why: The fake is set up to refuse loan1 with a reason.
The job only sees accepted or refused. B5's test proves that a failed connection comes back as refused, and B3's test proves how the job handles refused.

then.why: The reminders table must contain exactly one row, for loan2.
The event name is compared exactly.
The level is compared exactly.
loanId must equal loan1, which is not the member ID.
error must equal the exact reason the fake gave, so a generic message would fail.

then.part: and carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan2 must still be sent. This only catches a job that stops at the first refusal if loan1 is handled first; the test arranges that by lending loan1 earlier and with an earlier due date.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three loans are overdue: two are accepted and one is refused, and the job runs over all of them.

then.why: The last log entry must have exactly this event name.
The level is compared exactly.
sent must be 2. That differs from failed, so a missing or swapped count would fail.
failed must be 1.

given.why: The real client is called directly with a reminder.

then.why: The recorded method must be POST, and the handler only matches POST.
The handler is bound to the full NOTIFY_URL path and unhandled requests raise an error (http-interceptor.setup.ts:4), so a wrong host or path would make the request fail and the test with it.
The content-type must be exactly application/json, and the body is parsed as JSON.
The whole body is compared with toEqual, so a renamed or missing key would fail.
The template value is compared exactly.
The data object is compared exactly, keys and values.
202, 200 and 204 must each come back as accepted.
Only a 400 is tried. A client that refused only 4xx answers and accepted 5xx would pass, and B3's service test uses the fake client, not real HTTP.
A network error must come back as kind refused.

then.part: with a reason naming the status
then.why: The reason must contain "400".

then.part: or saying the API was unreachable
then.why: The reason must contain "unreachable".
